walkthroughs.body_html: Mussolini, a former socialist journalist, founded the Fasci di Combattimento in 1919. Exploiting fears of socialism, weak coalition governments and economic distress, the Fascist movement grew rapidly. The March on Rome of October 1922 prompted King Victor Emmanuel III to appoint Mussolini Prime Minister.

The Acerbo Law of 1923, the murder of Matteotti in 1924 and the Aventine secession allowed Mussolini to establish single-party rule by 1926. Censorship, OVRA secret police and the Special Tribunal repressed opposition; the Lateran Pacts of 1929 secured Catholic support; corporativism gave a veneer of economic modernisation.

Foreign adventures — Ethiopia (1935-36), intervention in Spain (1936-39) and alignment with Hitler — over-extended Italy. Disastrous campaigns in Greece, North Africa and the USSR plus the Allied invasion of Sicily led to Mussolini's dismissal in July 1943. Rescued by the Germans, he led the puppet Italian Social Republic before his execution by partisans in April 1945.
